issues.legal_issue: A High Court may disturb concurrent factual findings in a second appeal when those findings result from failure to consider relevant evidence or an essentially erroneous approach.
material_facts: The trial court and first appellate court found that the plaintiff was not ready and willing to perform the agreement.
The High Court considered notices stating that the plaintiff was ready and willing, as well as evidence that the plaintiff had funds available to perform.
The Supreme Court confirmed the High Court’s finding that the plaintiff was ready and willing and that the defendant was in breach.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was entitled to reappreciate the evidence and record proper findings because the concurrent findings were vitiated by non-consideration of relevant evidence.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 100 of the Code of Civil Procedure, a High Court hearing a second appeal is not precluded from recording proper findings where findings of fact are vitiated by non-consideration of relevant evidence or an essentially erroneous approach.

predicates.second_appeal: The proceeding was a second appeal from lower-court decisions.
predicates.concurrent_factual_findings: The trial court and first appellate court reached the same factual finding.
predicates.relevant_evidence_not_considered: The lower courts did not consider evidence relevant to the factual issue.

issues.definition: When a second appeal contains concurrent factual findings made without considering relevant evidence, the High Court may correct those findings.

issues.legal_issue: A notice returned after the addressee refuses to accept it may be presumed served, and its relevant averments may be treated as part of the pleading when relied on in the pleading.
material_facts: Before filing suit, the plaintiff sent two notices stating that he was ready and willing to perform the agreement.
The notices were returned unserved after the defendant refused to accept them.
The plaintiff referred to and relied on the notices in the suit.
issues.conclusion: The notices were presumed to have been served, and the High Court could rely on their averments as part of the plaint.
issues.legal_principle: Section 27 of the General Clauses Act, 1897 provides the basis for presuming service where a notice is refused; averments in notices referred to and relied on in the plaint may be treated as part of it.

predicates.specific_performance_suit: The claimant brought a suit seeking specific performance of an agreement.
predicates.notice_refused_by_addressee: The addressee refused to accept a notice sent by the claimant.
predicates.notice_relied_on_in_pleading: The claimant referred to and relied on the notice in the pleading.

issues.definition: In a specific-performance suit, a refused notice relied on in the pleading is treated as served, and its relevant averments are treated as pleading material.

issues.legal_issue: Compensation may be awarded in lieu of specific performance when the contract becomes incapable of performance without fault of the plaintiff.
material_facts: The plaintiff sued for specific performance and was found ready and willing to perform the agreement.
During the second appeal, the State acquired the property for a public purpose, making specific performance impossible.
The plaintiff had not caused the impossibility by choosing to make specific performance unavailable.
issues.conclusion: The plaintiff could receive compensation in lieu and substitution of specific performance despite the property’s acquisition.
issues.legal_principle: Section 21(2), (4) and (5) of the Specific Relief Act, 1963, including its explanation, permits compensation where specific performance becomes impossible without the plaintiff’s fault. Section 73 of the Contract Act governs assessment. The Court explained Ardeshir H. Mama v. Flora Sassoon, distinguished Piarey Lal v. Hori Lal, and disapproved the contrary reasoning in Mohamad Abdul Jabbar v. Lalmia. It distinguished Indian law from Lord Cairns’ Act, 1858, under which compensation was unavailable when performance became impossible.

predicates.specific_performance_suit: The claimant brought a suit seeking specific performance of a contract.
predicates.performance_became_impossible_without_pl: An event outside the claimant’s fault made performance of the contract impossible.
predicates.plaintiff_did_not_choose_impossibility: The claimant did not cause the impossibility by abandoning or otherwise choosing to make specific performance unavailable.

issues.definition: If performance becomes impossible without the claimant’s fault and the claimant did not choose that result, compensation may replace specific performance.

issues.legal_issue: A plaintiff may amend a specific-performance claim to seek compensation in addition to or in substitution for performance, while a conversion of the suit into a damages-only claim is subject to a different and less liberal amendment standard.
material_facts: The plaintiff had not specifically sought compensation in lieu of specific performance.
The contract became incapable of specific performance because the property was acquired during the proceedings.
The Supreme Court permitted an amendment to complete justice and provide compensation in substitution for performance.
issues.conclusion: The amendment to claim compensation in lieu of specific performance was permitted; the Court distinguished that amendment from one converting the suit into a damages-only action.
issues.legal_principle: The proviso to Section 21(5) of the Specific Relief Act, 1963 requires the court to allow, on just terms and at any stage, an amendment seeking compensation in addition to or in substitution for specific performance. A conversion into a claim for damages for breach is governed by Order 6 Rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure and is subject to less liberal standards; Section 73 of the Contract Act supplies the principles for assessing compensation.

predicates.specific_performance_suit: The claimant brought a suit seeking specific performance of a contract.
predicates.compensation_not_claimed_initially: The claimant did not include a claim for compensation in the original pleading.
predicates.amendment_seeks_compensation_with_perfor: The requested amendment adds compensation in addition to or in substitution for performance without converting the suit into a damages-only claim.

issues.definition: When a claimant in a specific-performance suit did not initially claim compensation but seeks to add it while retaining the performance claim, the amendment is allowed.

issues.legal_issue: Compensation for breach may be assessed by the ordinary contract-damages standard and, when the property has been acquired, by reference to the acquisition compensation, subject to appropriate deductions for the defendant’s expenditure and services.
material_facts: The property covered by the reconveyance agreement was acquired by the State, and compensation for the acquisition had been determined.
The defendant had spent time, money and effort pursuing the acquisition-compensation claims and had paid the consideration stipulated for reconveyance.

The Court used the acquisition compensation, with associated statutory payments, as the basis for the plaintiff’s recovery and allowed a deduction for the defendant’s services, expenditure and the reconveyance consideration.
issues.conclusion: Compensation was measured by the acquisition compensation and associated payments, less the amount allowed to the defendant for services, time, expenditure and the stipulated consideration.
issues.legal_principle: Section 21(4) of the Specific Relief Act, 1963 directs courts to apply Section 73 of the Contract Act when determining compensation. The English rule in Bain v. Fothergill, denying recovery for loss of bargain in the relevant circumstances, was held inapplicable. The Court referred to Pollock & Mulla on Contract and Nagardas v. Ahmedkhan in explaining the ordinary measure of damages for breach.

predicates.specific_performance_claim_rendered_impo: A claim for specific performance became impossible because the subject property was acquired.
predicates.acquisition_compensation_determined: The compensation payable for the acquisition had been determined.
predicates.defendant_incurred_claim_related_outlays: The defendant spent time, money or effort pursuing compensation for the acquired property or paid consideration under the contract.

issues.definition: When acquisition makes specific performance impossible and acquisition compensation is determined, compensation is based on that award, with an allowance for the defendant’s relevant outlays.
